 ORDER
This is the first application under Section 439 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
The applicant is implicated in connection with Crime No.395/2022 registered at Police Station Makdon, District Ujjain (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468 of the IPC.

The applicant is in custody since 12.01.2023.
2.

As per the prosecution, a written complaint was made by the complainant on 26.10.2021 to the effect that Nagar Parishad, Makdon, District Ujjain had invited tender on 07.09.2016 for auction of 44 shops.
In the tender the complainant had deposited a total sum of Rs.7,84,500/- by way of earnest money and had sought allotment of shop Nos.47 and 62.
The process of tender was cancelled due to which Nagar Parishad Makdon had to refund all the deposited amount to the prospective tenderers.

sentences.text: the amount which has to be refunded to him be instead refunded to co-accused.
Relying upon the said application and affidavit the amount has been paid to the co- accused persons.

On the allegation that an amount of Rs.2,92,000/- has been transferred in the account of applicant which ought to have been transferred to the complainant, the applicant has been implicated and arrested for the present offence.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
He was merely a muster employee and was acting on directions of his superior officer.
He has personally not been involved in the conspiracy whereby the amount of the complainant has been allegedly transferred.
The case is based upon documentary evidence which has already been collected by the prosecution and no recovery has to be made from the applicant.
His further custodial interrogation is no longer required.
On such grounds prayer for grant of bail to the applicant has been made.

4. The aforesaid prayer has been opposed by learned counsel for the respondent/State as well as learned counsel for the objector submitting that in view of the allegations levelled against the applicant, he is not entitled to be released on bail.
5. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and have perused the case diary.
6. The applicant is stated to be a muster employee in whose account the part of the fund of the complainant has been transferred.
The case is based upon documentary evidence which evidence is on record in view of which further custodial interrogation of the applicant does not appear to be necessary.
He is a Government servant and his custody may prove adverse to his service carrier.
The co-accused Kailashchandra who was disbursing authority has already been granted the benefit of anticipatory bail by this Court vide order dated 25.01.2022 passed in M.Cr.C. No.59037 of 2022.
Thus in my opinion the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
7. Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application filed by the applicant is allowed.

The applicant is directed to be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the Court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
8. The applicant shall appear before the trial Court and shall deposit a sum of Rs.3 Lakhs within a period of three months from today under protest.
In case of his failure to do so this order shall automatically come to an end.
9. This order shall be effective till the end of the trial, however, in case of bail jump, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
